name: fastapi_app_factory
description: Application-factory wiring. create_application(router: APIRouter) receives the router as a parameter and calls application.include_router(router) on it, so the app and the router it serves are connected only at the call site in src/main.py. Resolving the real URL requires following that call into the function. This is the layout benavlabs/FastAPI-boilerplate uses.
known_failing_reason: build_router_prefix_map() resolves include_router chains between module-level router variables, but here the app's include_router argument is a function parameter. Linking it to root_router requires interprocedural analysis: finding calls to create_application and reading the argument bound to `router`. Endpoints are currently reported as GET /orders/ and DELETE /orders/{order_id}, omitting /api/v1, and the documented endpoint is consequently misreported as a gap.
notes: Added after running against real repositories. The synthetic fixture fastapi_router_prefix used a literal prefix and no aliasing, so it passed while both full-stack-fastapi-template and FastAPI-boilerplate reported paths their services do not serve. Settings-constant prefixes and alias-imported routers are now fixed and covered by TestCrossFileRouterPrefixes; this factory pattern is not. Implementing it should make this case XPASS, at which point the flag comes off.
